name: Hollywood's Golden Age
description: The studio years, from silent comedy to Technicolor: the stars and directors who made the American film factory the world's main window on the movies.

checkpoints.name: Silent stars
checkpoints.note: Pickford, Chaplin and Keaton make a worldwide audience laugh without a word, and found studios of their own. In 1927 The Jazz Singer brings sound to the screen.

checkpoints.name: Sound and the studios
checkpoints.note: Talkies arrive and big studios such as MGM, Warner Bros. and Paramount sign stars such as Garbo, Bogart, Gable and Bette Davis. Hitchcock, Ford and Capra make a name, and Citizen Kane, The Wizard of Oz and Casablanca set the standard.

checkpoints.name: Postwar glamour
checkpoints.note: Colour, widescreen and television bring change. Monroe, Audrey Hepburn and Taylor are the new stars, Brando and Dean bring a rawer Method style of acting, and Wilder and Hitchcock make some of their most famous films, as Singin' in the Rain shows the musical at its best.

checkpoints.name: The studios fade
checkpoints.note: As television takes viewers and the old studio system breaks up, Sidney Poitier becomes the first Black man to win the Oscar for best actor in 1964, and New Hollywood directors take over with films such as The Godfather.
